# Energy table

<!-- Generated by src/test/java/buildcraftreforged/EnergyTableTest.java; do not edit by hand. -->

Every energy value of Buildcraft Reforged in Forge Energy (FE), with the BuildCraft 4.2.2 value in
Minecraft Joules (MJ) beside it in brackets. The conversion is fixed: **1 MJ = 10 FE**
(`docs/PLAN.md` section 7). The numbers are read from the code, the shipped data files and the config
defaults by `EnergyTableTest`, which fails the build when this file is out of date. Regenerate it with:

```bash
./gradlew test --tests buildcraftreforged.EnergyTableTest -PupdateEnergyTable
```

Two rules differ from 4.2.2 on purpose (decided 1 Nov 2026, `docs/PORTING-NOTES.md`, "Engine wrench and
engine Reason line"):

- **Weak engines drive any machine.** 4.2.2 refused an engine pulse below the receiver's minimum intake.
  An engine now waits for the smaller of the receiver's minimum and its own largest pulse, and the
  receiver takes a pulse below its minimum. Strong engines still wait for the minimum.
- **Perdition stops at the activation energy.** Perdition (the idle loss) never takes a machine below
  the energy one operation needs, so a weak engine's trickle builds up to it. Energy above it still
  decays as in 4.2.2.

Intake values are FE per call (per engine pulse or per pipe insert), not per tick. Perdition is FE per
tick. A machine works when its store holds at least its activation energy.

## Engines

An engine burns into its own store and sends one pulse each piston stroke, at most its largest pulse.
Engines chain: each also takes power from an engine or pipe behind it, between its minimum and maximum
intake, and keeps 95 % of it.

| Engine | Output, FE/t (MJ/t) | Largest pulse, FE (MJ) | Store, FE (MJ) | Minimum intake, FE (MJ) | Maximum intake, FE (MJ) | Perdition of the intake, FE/t (MJ/t) |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| Redstone engine | 0.5 (0.05) | 10 (1) | 1000 (100) | 0 (0) | 500 (50) | 0.1 (0.01) |
| Stirling engine | 3.33 to 10 (0.33 to 1) | 1000 (100) | 10 000 (1000) | 20 (2) | 2000 (200) | 0.1 (0.01) |
| Combustion engine | oil 30 (3), fuel 60 (6) | 5000 (500) | 100 000 (10 000) | 20 (2) | 20 000 (2000) | 0.1 (0.01) |

- The redstone engine's output is the value its GUI shows; while powered it adds 10 FE (1 MJ) to its
  store every 16 ticks and sends it as one pulse.
- The Stirling engine's output follows its store, between the two values shown.
- The combustion engine's output is the fuel's power per cycle (`data_maps/fluid/combustion_fuels.json`);
  a bucket burns for the fuel's burning time below, times the `fuel.oil.combustion` or
  `fuel.fuel.combustion` config value (defaults 1 and 1).
- An engine that is not redstone powered loses 10 FE (1 MJ) of its store per tick.

| Combustion fuel | Power per cycle, FE/t (MJ/t) | Burning time per bucket, ticks |
|---|---|---|
| oil | 30 (3) | 5000 |
| fuel | 60 (6) | 25 000 |

## Machines

The values at the default `mining.cost.multipler` of 1; the quarry's and mining well's values scale
with it.

| Machine | Minimum intake, FE (MJ) | Maximum intake, FE (MJ) | Activation energy, FE (MJ) | Store, FE (MJ) | Perdition, FE/t (MJ/t) | Cost per operation, FE (MJ) |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| Quarry, building its frame | 500 (50) | 1000 (100) | 250 (25) | 150 000 (15 000) | 20 (2) | 250 (25) per frame block |
| Quarry, digging | 1000 (100) | 5000 (500) | 640 (64) | 150 000 (15 000) | 20 (2) | 640 (64) per block |
| Mining well | 1000 (100) | 1000 (100) | 640 (64) | 10 000 (1000) | 10 (1) | 640 (64) per block |
| Pump | 10 (1) | 150 (15) | 100 (10) | 1000 (100) | 0.1 (0.01) | 100 (10) per fluid block |
| Refinery | 500 (50) | 1500 (150) | 250 (25) | 10 000 (1000) | 10 (1) | per recipe, below |
| Filler | 300 (30) | 500 (50) | 250 (25) | 1000 (100) | 10 (1) | 250 (25) per block |
| Laser | 250 (25) | 1500 (150) | 250 (25) | 10 000 (1000) | 5 (0.5) | sends at most 40 (4) per tick |

The laser tables have no intake of their own: they store what lasers send them.

| Laser table | Cost per operation, FE (MJ) |
|---|---|
| Assembly table | per recipe, below |
| Advanced crafting table | 5000 (500) per craft |

## Power pipes

The `transport.tiers.<material>.powerPerTick` config defaults. Power pipes store nothing; this is what
one pipe carries per tick. The tier ladder replaced the 4.2.2 pipes (`docs/PLAN.md` section 8), so the
last column is the 4.2.2 cap of the power pipe of the same material, where there was one.

| Material | Tier | Throughput, FE/t (MJ/t) | 4.2.2 cap, MJ/t |
|---|---|---|---|
| Wood | 1 | 80 (8) | 32 |
| Stone | 2 | 160 (16) | 16 |
| Iron | 3 | 320 (32) | 128 |
| Copper | 4 | 640 (64) | none |
| Gold | 5 | 1280 (128) | 256 |
| Quartz | 6 | 2560 (256) | 64 |
| Diamond | 7 | 5120 (512) | 1024 |
| Emerald | 8 | 10 240 (1024) | none |
| Netherite | 9 | 20 480 (2048) | none |
| Ender | 10 | 40 960 (4096) | none |

4.2.2's cobblestone power pipe (8 MJ/t) has no successor.
